Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] 504s and client 429s — production API timeouts

Quick update from infra traces and a low-level dump I pulled:
- Symptoms: high request queueing on the serving runtime, KV-cache eviction pressure correlated with short-lived prefix cache churn.
- Observed behavior: continuous batching routine is occasionally spinning up very large batches when KV cache misses spike; this causes head-of-line blocking and a backlog of inflight requests => timeouts and 504s.
- Root cause hypothesis: an edge-case in the KV-cache tracking when many concurrent short sequences (ParkView usage pattern in the morning) cause cache thrash. The batching code then expands batch windows to keep throughput and ends up increasing latency for everyone.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (in order):
1) Toggle per-customer aggressive-batching feature OFF for ParkView (per-route flag) — low risk, should reduce batching window size.
2) Apply a temporary rate-limit for concurrent generation calls from ParkView SDKs to avoid retry storms (10 qps).
3) Hotfix: stop the KV-cache eviction metric from triggering batch expansion until we push a robust patch. I'll prepare a candidate diff but need signoff.

I've attached a brief trace and a candidate patch outline. If we need to roll a hotfix, I'll coordinate with Stephanie on canary cadence.

(Attachment: candidate_patch_kv_cache.diff — text/diff)

— Marissa (Infra/Serving Runtime)
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ops@parkview.ai

Date: 2026-05-07T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] 504s and client 429s — production API timeouts

Agree with Marissa. I've started a canary rollout of a throttled batching configuration for ParkView's model endpoints and lowered the batch_size cap on the affected pools. Early telemetry (9:03-9:10) shows a drop in queue length and error rate trending down to ~3-4%.

I'll continue monitoring; if stable for 15m we'll keep the config and prepare a patch deployment to prod.

Also: Rishi — can you prepare an exec note summarizing customer impact and ask for any compensation approval? ParkView is Tier-1.

— Stephanie
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: 2026-05-07T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] 504s and client 429s — executive summary for ParkView outage

Dylan / Evelyn —

Draft executive summary:
- Impact: ParkView experienced a production outage beginning 08:10 PT causing elevated 504s and 429s; peak error rate ~18%; affected sessions primarily short-sequence high-concurrency workloads.
- Cause: a KV-cache eviction/thrashing interaction with our dynamic batching heuristic led to large batch windows and head-of-line latency. Root-cause fix: patch the KV-cache tracking to avoid spuriously expanding batch windows and add stronger backpressure to batching controller.
- Mitigation performed: immediately disabled aggressive-batching for ParkView, applied per-customer concurrent call throttle, lowered batch caps on affected pools; error rate reduced to ~2-4% within ~25 minutes.
- Next steps: push hotfix in 3-step canary (staging -> limited prod -> full prod), follow-up postmortem with timeline, propose goodwill credit (3 days) and account-level telemetry export for ParkView.

If approved, Evelyn, I'll send this to Amit + legal/account while Marissa and Stephanie complete the patch.
